---
name: accept
description: "Run the acceptance scenarios on fresh fixtures, show the evidence to the owner and record the decision."
argument-hint: "[accept | reject spec | reject build]"
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

<!-- Generated by plugin-tools build-ports from commands/accept.md. -->
Follow the `logic-fabric-dataverse:testing` skill. Stage 6 (Acceptance) for the change in `logic-fabric/.active`.

1. Check `status.yaml`: `stage: acceptance`, and no open blocker or major finding other than those the owner chose
   to accept as risks at review.
2. Run every test of the change and the regression set on fresh fixtures (retired cases are skipped), and check that the exported sources in
   `artifacts/` match the environment (`get` with `include: ["source"]`).
3. Write `acceptance.md`: each acceptance criterion with its evidence (records and their links, outputs), the test
   totals and the review verdict.
4. Walk the owner through it, then ask Foundry for the owner's decision: `release`, `action: "approve"`,
   `options.gate: "acceptance"`, `options.text` the full `acceptance.md` as saved, the `changeId` and `project`.
   Foundry asks the owner, not you: accept, or send the change back to its build or to its spec, with a reason. A
   client without that dialog gets Foundry's approval page, as for the spec and plan (see the authoring skill).
   Accepting also accepts the review's open findings as risks, recorded with the owner as their approver. If a
   blocker is open, Foundry first answers with a link for a reviewer (the Logic Fabric Foundry Reviewer role): give
   it to the user to pass on (you can't answer it). The reviewer accepts the blockers as risks there, or sends the
   change back to its build. When the user says it's answered, ask Foundry again.
5. Record what Foundry reports, then stop:
   - **Accepted**: record `accepted_by` and `accepted_at` in `status.yaml` and `acceptance.md`, set `stage: accepted`,
     merge the glossary additions into `logic-fabric/glossary.md`, copy the change's tests into
     `logic-fabric/baseline/tests/` (the regression set), update the as-built requirements document with the
     `logic-fabric-dataverse:documenter` agent (`logic_fabric_documenter` in Codex), clear `logic-fabric/.active`, tell the owner the change is ready
     for ALM (export the solution and run the pipeline), and offer, as a choice in your question tool, to commit the
     workflow's files ("Offer the next step" in the authoring skill says how). Foundry has closed
     it: work after that, undoing it included, is a new change.
   - **Sent back to the build or the spec**: record the reason in `acceptance.md`, and `rejected_by` and
     `rejected_reason` (a new reason) in `status.yaml` in the same edit that sets the stage back to `build` or `spec`;
     the stage hook refuses the move without them. Sent back to the spec, Foundry has cleared the spec and plan
     approvals: both are approved again before anything is built. Offer the next step as a choice in your question
     tool: the build or the spec.
   - **No decision**: nothing was recorded; the change is still waiting for acceptance.

Only when Foundry answers that this environment doesn't keep the stages of changes, or can't ask the owner at all,
take the decision in the session (one question to the user), say in `build-log.md` that Foundry didn't record it, and use
the argument: `accept` records the acceptance as above; `reject spec` or `reject build`, only when the owner rejects,
records the reason and moves the stage back as above. Never record a decision the owner didn't make.
